title: An R-based method for producing river bathymetry from sonar sensor data
author: Redana, Carrero-Carralero

steps.title: Install app and configure sonar
steps.instruction: Install the Fisher Deep app on a smartphone, launch it, and use it to establish a Wi‑Fi link (up to 80 m, extendable to 150 m) with the Deeper Chirp+2; customize beam angle as needed and set the acquisition mode to either “Bait Boat” or “Bank”, which enable the built‑in GNSS for positioning.

steps.title: Prepare phone and initialize sonar
steps.instruction: Put the phone in airplane mode to avoid Wi‑Fi interruptions, place the sonar in the water, and keep it submerged until the green GNSS indicator appears (≈1 minute) to ensure a stable GNSS lock; the sonar will automatically start recording once the water depth reaches at least 15 cm and data will be displayed on the app.

steps.title: Select acquisition mode and conduct survey
steps.instruction: Choose the desired output mode and follow the corresponding field procedure:

substeps.instruction: Bathymetry‑map mode – move the sonar continuously so that its path homogeneously covers the whole target area.

Cross‑section mode – follow a single transect; if multiple transects are required, keep the sonar out of the water for at least one minute between each transect to allow the algorithm to separate them, then re‑stabilize the GNSS lock before the next pass. The same transect may be repeated without interruption to improve accuracy. Record the distance from each river bank to the first and last sonar measurement (minimum depth 15 cm).

steps.title: Optional: integrate external GNSS receiver
steps.instruction: If higher positioning accuracy is needed, connect an external GNSS receiver/antenna (e.g., Android device running Open GEA or GNSS Logger) to record raw GNSS data, later process to RINEX and optionally apply PPK correction; after the survey produce a CSV file containing latitude, longitude and UNIX timestamp columns for the external GNSS points.

steps.title: Verify data storage and file handling
steps.instruction: During acquisition the app saves data locally and uploads them to the free cloud account (https://maps.fishdeeper.com); the resulting file *bathymetry.csv* contains columns latitude (°), longitude (°), depth (m), temperature (°C) and time (Unix). Latitude/longitude are logged at 1 Hz under optimal satellite coverage, while depth and temperature are logged at 15 Hz. If all recordings span less than 24 h (even from different locations) they are automatically merged into a single CSV file.

description: The methodology here presented allows to produce bathymetry map or cross-sections of river/channel from low-cost sonar data, specifically the Deeper Chirp+2. In addition, it allows to integrate external GNSS receiver to improve sonar point geolocation. All the data elaboration is concentrated in three R-based functions. The methods have been successfully implemented to produce extensive bathymetric maps in tropical context (Redana et al., unpublished) and reconstruct river cross-sections for flow estimation in alpine environment (Carrero-Carralero et al., unpublished). These confirm the robustness of the methodology here proposed, along with the flexibility of the equipment to be deployed in different environmental contexts and experimental setting (Fig. 12).Fig. 12Applications of sonar recording in different data collection setting A) Manually recorded in an alpine river B) attached to an extendable arm on a speedboat during a bathymetric reconstruction in a tropical river.Fig. 12 Nonetheless, the overall accuracy of the bathymetric reconstruction itself largely depends on two aspects: (I) the quality of the original data (i.e., the accuracy of the Deeper Chirp+2 in water depth estimation) and (II) the performance of the interpolation. (I) and (II) concur and interact to define the final accuracy of the bathymetric map estimated with Eqs. (5)–(8) (results provided by the “bathymery_map” function, see 3.2 step V). It can be hard to quantify the specific contribution to the final error of (I) and (II), especially in extensive data collection for large or deep water bodies. The performance of the sonar in the water depth estimation, can vary according to water condition (e.g., turbidity) and experiment setting (e.g., collection speed). Thus we suggest to run some test, prior to the proper data collection, to estimate the accuracy of the Deeper Chirp+2 in environmental and experimental condition as similar as possible to the actual survey.
